why_this_file_exists: The slice-63 pack is the SLICE-61 tree: every artefact slice 62 produced is absent from it, and the baseline suite failed the same eight tests for the same reason. Recorded without accusation — a tree can be assembled from the wrong parent — but the work is not in the pack, so this slice either re-derives it or proceeds without it. This file says exactly what was brought back and pins every byte of it. EDGE.md §46a, §46b.

apparatus.why: NOT souvenirs. Without a forward-window restriction there is no forward window to score, and without the prefix invariant the suite is red on a corpus that grew legitimately. These are the apparatus that makes slice 63 computable at all.
apparatus.restored_byte_identically: 9 of 9 restored byte-identically; 1 subsequently amended in slice 63 and recorded under amended_in_slice63 with both digests
apparatus.note: Copied, not rewritten. A re-implementation that happened to agree would be a second opinion presented as the original; these digests let a reader confirm they are the same bytes.

tests/test_slice62_forward_extension.py.why: As written the test excluded callers named `slice62_*` — a SLICE NUMBER standing in for a ROLE. Slice 63's own forward-shadow tool, whose entire job is to call `restrict_flags_to_forward`, therefore failed it the moment it existed. Adding `slice63_*` to the exclusion would have been the same mistake one slice later.
tests/test_slice62_forward_extension.py.what_changed: The rule now names the role: the helper may be called by the module that defines it and by any `tools/slice<N>_forward_shadow.py`. Anything else still fails, and six named scoring modules are asserted absent by name, so the check cannot pass by sweeping nothing.
tests/test_slice62_forward_extension.py.strength: STRICTLY STRONGER. The old form let ANY file named slice62_* call the helper, including a hypothetical slice62_edge_measurement.py. The new form permits one filename shape in one directory and names the scoring modules that must never appear.
tests/test_slice62_forward_extension.py.note: A TEST is a living document; a dated ARTEFACT is not. That distinction is the one slices 54, 57 and 62 each had to unpick. No dated record was touched: artifacts/slice62_*.json and STAGE1_VERDICT_SLICE62.md still carry their as-restored digests, listed under dated_records.

dated_records.why: These describe measurements that were actually taken, on a corpus state that existed. They are copied byte-for-byte with their original git_commit fields intact.
dated_records.why_not_regenerated: Re-running the slice-62 tools today would produce files that LOOK like slice-62 records and are not — the precise substitution §45c had to unpick for slice61_data_freshness.json. Doing it deliberately would be worse than doing it by accident.
dated_records.now_disagree_with_disk: slice62_data_freshness.json records after_t1_funding = 5; the disk now holds 6. That is correct dated-artefact behaviour, not drift: the file records what was true when it was written.

evidence_the_pack_is_the_slice61_tree.method: Whole-file digests, not a file listing. Three files that slice 62 modified hash to their SLICE-61 values.

baseline_suite.note: Eight tests failing identically is not a coincidence; it is the same tree meeting a grown corpus for the second time.

the_restored_invariant_was_not_refitted: The restored apparatus passed against the slice-63 corpus WITHOUT modification — 238 passed, 1 skipped across the four affected test files on first run. An invariant that had been quietly fitted to slice 62's numbers would have needed a nudge here. It needed none.
